title: Emergency operator escalation: RBACv2 timebound escalation, KMS soft-failover, and provenance audit
author: Marisol Vega
merge_outcome: Squash merged into main after CI green and two approvals
description: Motivation: incidents where a primary KMS region experienced transient network partitions exposed a gap: operator runbooks allowed manual cross-region key use without formal RBAC timebound escalation and produced sparse audit provenance. This PR adds a guarded emergency escalation flow: 1) RBACv2 timebound escalation role templates that grant ephemeral operator privileges for a bounded window with explicit justification metadata; 2) a KMS soft-failover adapter that prefers local region providers but can route to a vetted secondary provider under strictly-audited conditions; 3) audit provenance-v2 enrichment that records the escalation justification, region decision, attestations and a cryptographic event tag to enable downstream validators to reconstruct the decision path. The implementation emphasizes minimal blast radius and auditability rather than permanent privilege widening.

review_comments: Diego Ramos: Please add a short TTL fail-safe on issued escalation tokens independent of the controller (done in issuer_service.go, PTAL).
Anya Kapoor: Audit payloads look large — can we strip sensitive plaintext and use a provenance-hash with a minimal envelope (switched to hash envelope; kept signed metadata).
Benji Park: Gate the feature behind a default-disabled cluster flag; require manual enable in Dedicated/Private (added helm flag and console guard).
Marisol Vega (author): Addressed comments: TTL added, provenance hash envelope implemented, helm/enforcer flag added, updated docs and migration notes.
notes_on_design: Timebound roles: issued via the existing RBACv2 operator token flow but scoped with a new escalation_reason field and an explicit expiry claim; the projector denies renewal beyond the original window.

KMS soft-failover: adapter implements provider preference list, health scoring, and an explicit operator-acknowledged fallback route captured in the audit envelope; no automatic cross-region key wrapping without an operator-issue escalation token.

Audit provenance-v2: emits compact signed event tags (sha256 over canonicalized decision + nonce) plus a minimal envelope with attestation pointers; downstream indexer can expand pointers when needed.
Operational controls: helm/console feature flag, per-tenant allowlist for fallback providers, and rate-limited escalation issuance to prevent abuse.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: operator misuse to bypass residency policies. Mitigation: timebound tokens, rate limits, and post-facto automatic revocation if anomalous patterns are detected.
Risk: audit volume increase. Mitigation: provenance envelope is hash-first with optional expanded payload retention behind an admin data-retention setting.
Risk: fallback provider compulsion by regulator. Mitigation: per-tenant allowlist and policy evaluation that blocks fallback when tenant policy denies cross-region wrap.
testing_summary: Unit tests: 98% coverage for new issuer logic and adapter decision tree.
Integration: kms soft-failover exercised against a local mock provider and a staged external provider; e2e test simulates primary region partition and verifies operator flow and audit records.
Chaos: brief network partition scenario using perf-canary harness validated automatic fallback suppressed without escalation token.
deploy_and_migration: Feature is behind helm flag 'operatorEscalation.enabled' (default: false) and console toggle for Dedicated/Private customers.
Migration: migration job creates new RBACv2 escalation templates and seeds an allowlist table for fallback providers; migration id: 20251110-escalation-seed.
Rollout: recommended staged rollout - enable in internal staging, then beta tenants with security SRE oversight before general availability.

release_notes: Introduce guarded operator escalation for RBACv2, a KMS soft-failover adapter (disabled by default), and provenance-v2 audit enrichment. Admins must enable operator escalation explicitly; follow the rollout guide in docs/security/operator-escalation.md.
